questions.question: What is the typical structure of the oral English exam?
options: Preparation time, a presentation (5-10 min) and a conversation with examiners (10-15 min)
A written test followed by a quiz
A group debate lasting two hours
Only a listening test
questions.explanation: The oral exam typically has 30-45 minutes of preparation, a 5-10 minute presentation and a 10-15 minute conversation.

questions.question: How should you use notes during your presentation?
options: Speak from notes rather than reading a full script aloud
Read every word from a manuscript
Use no preparation at all
Hand your notes to the examiner
questions.explanation: Speaking from keyword notes keeps your delivery natural; reading aloud weakens communication.

questions.question: What should you do if you do not understand an examiner's question?
options: Ask for clarification
Stay silent until they move on
Answer a different question
End the exam
questions.explanation: Listening carefully and asking for clarification is expected — it shows genuine communication skills.

questions.question: Which criteria are you assessed on in the oral exam?
options: Content, language quality, communication ability and structure
Clothing, posture, punctuality and handwriting
Speed of speech only
The length of your presentation only
questions.explanation: Assessment covers content/knowledge, language (vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation), communication and coherence.

questions.question: Which preparation strategies does the chapter recommend?
options: Recording yourself, simulating exam conditions and getting peer feedback
Memorising one answer for all questions
Avoiding speaking practice to stay fresh
Practising only silently in your head
questions.explanation: Recording yourself, realistic practice runs and peer feedback are effective ways to prepare for the oral exam.
